messages:
Nina (support): heads-up — several EU customers (Acme, MedTechX) opened tickets about high latency and intermittent 502/503s since ~08:02 UTC. They all report requests ending up in us-west. Tickets: #4321 #4322. Paging @oncall and @Alex for triage.

monitoring-bot: alert: healthcheck flip detected for pool eu-west-1: probe failures observed 08:01:58 -> 08:03:12 (5m window threshold exceeded). Automated failover to fallback-tier us-west-2 executed.

Alex (eng-sre): on it. Any deploys or config changes in the last hour?

Nina (support): no deploys on our side. Customers pasted a curl reproduction showing headers:
```
$ curl -i -H 'Host: api.redwood.ai' https://eu-api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
HTTP/2 200
date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 08:05:12 GMT
server: redwood-edge
X-Region: us-west-2
via: proxy-usw2
content-type: application/json
```
They explicitly see X-Region: us-west-2 while hostname is eu-api.

Sasha (platform): I can see some oddness in the probe state timeline — a handful of health agents in eu returned transient failures right before the routing decision. There was also a NAT rotation for a subset of eu edges at ~07:58 that coincides. Might be TTL or probe source IP flip.

Alex (eng-sre): looking at request logs now. Querying traces around 07:55-08:10. If you have trace ids, drop them.

Nina (support): trace ids from customer: trc_abc123 and trc_def456. Also they reported 401s for some requests that later succeeded after retry — looks like auth tokens got rejected on the fallback region.

Alex (eng-sre): interesting — fallback to us-west shouldn't change auth validation, but we do have region-scoped session cookie validation in the token backend (introduced last year). If the fallback edge forwards to a different token verifier cluster that didn't receive the most recent key rotation, that could explain transient 401s. Sasha, any KMS/key rollout activities?

Sasha (platform): no KMS rotations logged in the control plane during that window. But there was a partial key sync lag (replica lag) between token-verifier clusters in eu and global clusters; sync lag peaked ~2m at 07:59. Combined with failover, some verifiers may have rejected tokens briefly.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot: no recent deploys. Routing-config: no manual changes. Healthcheck-config: eu probe interval 8s, failure threshold 3.

Alex (eng-sre): hypothesis: health agents (eu) started returning transient failures due to NAT/public IP rotation; control plane marked pool degraded and routed traffic to fallback (usw2). Because the token verifier in the fallback path had a small key-sync lag, some sessions were rejected causing 401s, contributing to noise and customer confusion. The root symptom customers saw was 'wrong region / slow' b/c requests had extra cross-region hop + some auth retries.

Nina (support): customers complaining about billing hits from retries and request duplication. They're asking for hotfix and reimbursement path.

Alex (eng-sre): immediate actions:
1) Temporarily pin routing affinity for eu-api host to eu-west-1 for the affected accounts for the next 2 hours to stop cross-region routing. (I'll open a route pin request).
2) Restart healthcheck agent service on the eu edge nodes that had NAT rotation to clear bad probe state.
3) Force key-sync for token-verifier replicas and monitor for rejection rate drop.
4) Collect full traces for trc_abc123/trc_def456 and attach to tickets.

Sasha (platform): I'll trigger the agent restart and kick key-sync. Also will add a short instrumentation patch to log probe source IPs for 24h so we can correlate NAT rotation windows.

Nina (support): I notified the customers that we're investigating and put the pin in place for their orgs. They want a short postmortem and billing remediation.

Alex (eng-sre): quick repro step for the team to validate routing header: run `curl -sI https://eu-api.redwood.ai/v1/health | grep X-Region` before and after the pin. Expected: before incident you might see us-west-2 if failover active; after pin: eu-west-1. Also check `x-request-trace-id` header in responses.

Sasha (platform): done: restarted agents on nodes eu-edge-{12,14,19}. Key sync forced; verifier rejection rate dropped from 2.4% -> 0.1% in 6m. Instrumentation logs enabled.

monitoring-bot: info: routing-affinity pins applied for orgs: acme, medtechx. Healthcheck success rates restored to 99.8% for eu pool.

Alex (eng-sre): good progress. Next steps: postmortem with timeline (include NAT rotation job, probe failure cascade, key-sync lag, and routing policy behavior). Also propose improving probe resilience to source-ip rotation (accept short source changes) and adding a pre-failover sniff step to validate token-verifier sync before cross-region failover.

Nina (support): I'll coordinate the customer comms and billing remediation doc. Will attach runbook steps so support can act faster next time.

Sasha (platform): logging note: saved sample pcap and probe logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/2168880000/ for the postmortem.

Alex (eng-sre): thanks — I'll follow up in incident channel with final timeline and owner assignments. Closing this Slack thread for support escalation; ongoing ops work tracked in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
